'''James H. Harrington III''' (born November 15, 1971), professionally known as '''Jay Harrington''', is an American actor and director. He is known for his role as the title character in the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] sitcom ''[[Better Off Ted]]'' (2009–2010), and as Sgt. David "Deacon" Kay in ''[[S.W.A.T. (2017 TV series)|S.W.A.T.]]'' from 2017 to 2025.

==Early life==
Harrington was born and raised in [[Wellesley, Massachusetts]] to Judy and Terry Harrington. He has two brothers, actor Adam and Matt.  As a child, his family spent summers on Cape Cod up the road from The Harwich Junior Theater. He attended [[Wellesley High School]]<ref>Ellis, Carolyn S. [http://www.wellesleywestonmagazine.com/fall09/hollywood.htm "Wellesley and Weston Grads Find Success on the West Coast"], ''WellesleyWeston Online'', 14 August 2009.</ref> and then studied theater at [[Syracuse University]].<ref>Herbert, Geoff. [http://www.syracuse.com/entertainment/index.ssf/2013/10/taye_diggs_jay_harrington_syracuse_university_orange_central.html "Actors Taye Diggs, Jay Harrington celebrate Syracuse University homecoming"], ''Syracuse.com'', 5 October 2013. Last accessed 11 April 2016.</ref>

==Career==
Harrington has been featured as Dr. Simon O'Keefe on the [[The WB Television Network|WB]] drama ''[[Summerland (TV series)|Summerland]]'', FBI Special Agent Paul Ryan on [[Fox Broadcasting Company|FOX]]'s short-lived ''[[The Inside (TV series)|The Inside]]'', and Steve on [[NBC]]'s version of ''[[Coupling (American TV series)|Coupling]]''. He appeared in a recurring role on the police drama series ''[[The Division]]''. He has also had roles on ''[[A.U.S.A.]]'', ''[[The Shield]]'', ''[[Time of Your Life (American TV series)|Time of Your Life]]'', ''[[Private Practice (TV series)|Private Practice]]'', and ''[[Burn Notice]]''.

In 2006, Harrington began appearing as Dr. Ron McCready on the series ''[[Desperate Housewives]]''. He starred as Ted Crisp in the comedy series ''[[Better Off Ted]]'' from March 2009 to January 2010. He had a recurring role in Season 4 of the [[TV Land]] comedy series ''[[Hot in Cleveland]]''. In 2014, he co-starred on the short-lived [[USA Network]] comedy series ''[[Benched (TV series)|Benched]]''. In 2017, he had a guest role on ''[[Suits (American TV series)|Suits]]'' as Mark Meadows, Donna's ex-boyfriend. He starred as Sergeant II David "Deacon" Kay on [[S.W.A.T. (2017 TV series)|''S.W.A.T.'']], based on the 1975 television series and 2003 movie of the same name, and was a series regular for all eight seasons.<ref>{{cite web|work=People.com|title=S.W.A.T. Finally Comes to an Explosive End After Cancellation Drama: How Shemar Moore's Team Bid Farewell in Series Finale|first=Esther|last=Kang|url=https://people.com/swat-series-finale-how-it-ended-shemar-moore-11736992|date=May 16, 2025|accessdate=June 4, 2025}}</ref> 

Harrington has appeared in films such as ''[[American Reunion]]'' (with his character again – like in ''Desperate Housewives'' – being called "Dr. Ron"), ''[[Whatever It Takes (2000 film)|Whatever It Takes]]'', ''[[Anywhere but Here (film)|Anywhere but Here]]'', ''Catalina Trust'', ''A Little Inside'', and ''Partner(s)''. He has also performed on stage, starring as Jack in ''Boy's Life'' and appearing in the [[off-Broadway]] productions ''[[Barefoot in the Park]]'' and ''[[Tony and Tina's Wedding]]'', Harrington is an avid sports fan who plays in the Entertainment League, a private celebrity basketball league (formerly the NBA-E League), and skates for a local amateur ice hockey team.
